text:
inc-bot: PAGE: oncall-sre alerted - elevated 5xx from gateway layer (api-gw) to model-serving. Severity: P1. Affected paths: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. Error profile: 502/504/timeouts.

oncall-sre-raj: I'm on it. Seeing spike started ~10:02 UTC, sustained error rate ~18% on prod-us-east-1. Routing shows a high tail at kv-cache lookups for prefix-store.

emma-platform: logged the incident in pagerduty. Customer impact: multiple PLG users hitting 5xx. Support is getting noisy.

oliver-runtime: quick dump: many downstream servers returning 5xx when they try to read prefix index. Suspicion: shard-level KV eviction / corruption causing timeouts on lookup. Latency on kv-read RPCs jumps from 5ms -> 2000ms.

tara-support: customer-reported errors for streaming completions. They see 'gateway timeout' in SDK. Which customers are we flagging for immediate outreach?

kevin-customer: @tara-support this is us — our prod queries got ~30% errors. Our fallback to smaller model helped but UX degraded. Would appreciate ETA.

oncall-sre-raj: noted @kevin-customer. We'll give rolling updates. First plan: confirm whether KV prefix shards show eviction storm or index corruption. Querying metrics and top-errors now.

maria-eng-ml: adding logs from model-side: logs show KV read failures with code 503 and 'prefix not found' for keys that should exist. Also see rehydration attempts. Could be TTL drift + aggressive compaction.

oliver-runtime: Command I'm running: ```for s in $(kubectl get pods -l app=kv-prefix -o name); do kubectl exec $s -- curl -sS localhost:9100/metrics | grep kv_prefix_errors || true; done``` Getting lots of 'kv_prefix_eviction' spikes.

oncall-sre-raj: good. If eviction count spikes correlate with 5xx timeline, mitigation options: 1) throttle eviction workers, 2) fail open (serve without prefix cache) for latency-sensitive routes, 3) roll a config to reduce retention/compaction adjustments.

emma-platform: rolling a feature-flag toggle available for 'prefix-cache-bypass' per-route. We can flip for /v1/generate in us-east-1 for immediate relief. Would cut unit-cost but reduce some performance.

tara-support: please flip now — customers above SLO thresholds. Need a quick note to support and to customers impacted.

oncall-sre-raj: @emma-platform please toggle bypass for prod-us-east-1 /v1/generate. Also add rate limit to bursty clients to avoid exacerbating backend pressure.

emma-platform: toggled prefix-cache-bypass=true for route /v1/generate in us-east-1. Pushing now.

inc-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: prefix-cache-bypass toggled by emma-platform at 10:14 UTC.

oliver-runtime: monitoring… baseline error rate dropped from 18% -> 7% in 90s for /v1/generate. /v1/embeddings still elevated.

oncall-sre-raj: For embeddings route we don't have bypass yet. Could we extend bypass to embeddings while we debug the KV slice?

emma-platform: can do, but need confirmation on long-term: bypass means more compute and higher tail latency for some requests. Are we OK for short window?

oncall-sre-raj: short window OK. Let's do embeddings too. Flip in 2m.

emma-platform: flipped embeddings bypass at 10:17 UTC.

oliver-runtime: embeddings error rate down to 4% now. System is stabilizing. Still seeing a handful of 5xx from nodes that hit large read batches.

maria-eng-ml: pulling a sample trace: request id abc123 shows kv-shard-7 returning inconsistent index version. The shard shows compaction job ran at 09:59 and TTL window misapplied by 1s across replicas. Not huge but caused race leading to missing prefix entries on read.

oncall-sre-raj: that points to a TTL drift bug in compaction/coordination. Mitigations: 1) disable aggressive compaction on shard-7 and neighbors, 2) restart the shard process to force a consistent snapshot, 3) schedule a controlled rehydrate run to repopulate missing prefixes. Which is safest?

oliver-runtime: safest is to reduce compaction concurrency and rehydrate. Restarting could cause more evictions temporarily. I suggest: pause compactions for affected shard group, kick rehydrate, keep bypass on, and watch error rates.

emma-platform: I can pause scheduled compaction via config: `kv.compaction.concurrency=0` for shard group. Applying now to us-east-1 clusters.

inc-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: kv.compaction.concurrency set to 0 in prod-us-east-1 by emma-platform at 10:25 UTC.

oncall-sre-raj: triggering rehydrate job to fetch prefixes from cold-store for affected shards. Command: `./admin rehydrate-prefixes --shard-group us-east-1-a --since 10:00`

oliver-runtime: rehydrate job started. Progress looks healthy, we have backfill rate ~5000 prefixes/s.

kevin-customer: thanks for the update. Any risk of data loss?

oncall-sre-raj: no data loss expected — missing prefixes are local cache entries; cold-store is authoritative. Rehydrate repopulates. While bypass is on, requests may be slightly slower but should succeed.

maria-eng-ml: also creating a regression test to reproduce TTL drift in the compaction coordinator. We'll push to staging asap.

oliver-runtime: note: a few nodes are still returning 5xx with 'kv replica timeout' — I plan a rolling restart of pods with >95th percentile kv lookup latency. Reasonable?

oncall-sre-raj: yes, do rolling restart with maxUnavailable=1 to avoid capacity hole. Coordinate with emma so bypass stays active during restarts.

emma-platform: acknowledged. Bypass will remain true until we confirm rehydrate completed and error rates stable for 15m.

inc-bot: ACTION: emma-platform to maintain bypass for 15m post-rehydrate. oliver-runtime to perform rolling restart.

oliver-runtime: initiating rolling restart at 10:38. Command: `kubectl rollout restart statefulset/kv-prefix -n prod --selector=shard-group=us-east-1-a`

(rolled 1/6) ... (rolled 6/6)

oliver-runtime: restarts complete at 10:45. Latency and error rates within normal bounds now.

oncall-sre-raj: monitoring shows error rate down to 1.2% cluster-wide, and essentially 0.3% for routes that had bypass enabled. Rehydrate at 98% complete.

emma-platform: I'm starting to remove bypass for /v1/generate from us-east-1 in a canary fashion: route 10% traffic back to cache path.

oliver-runtime: canary looks good for 10 minutes. No spike. Increasing to 50%.

oncall-sre-raj: hold 50% for 10m. If stable, roll to 100% and then remove embeddings bypass.

kevin-customer: thanks team — errors are gone for us. Appreciate the rapid follow-through.

maria-eng-ml: postmortem notes: root cause likely TTL drift during compaction due to clock jitter + compaction coordinator bug. Short-term fix: compaction concurrency limiter and rehydrate. Long-term: add stricter vector clock checks and regression test for TTL boundaries.

oncall-sre-raj: postmortem owners: maria (root cause & fix), oliver (runtime restart procedure & metrics), emma (route-level bypass playbook). I'll file incident ticket and link runbook.

inc-bot: INCIDENT: updated status -> mitigated at 11:05 UTC. Severity reduced to P2 pending postmortem.

emma-platform: support note prepared and sent to impacted customers including @kevin-customer.

oncall-sre-raj: thanks all. We'll keep a watch for 1h. If any reoccurrence, escalate immediately.

tara-support: closing loop with customers. Good job everyone. :tada:
